title: Recovery-inventory contract and coverage protocol
description:
Objective: land the cursor/incarnation-bound recovery-window inventory CONTRACT and COVERAGE PROTOCOL, plus the aggregate API that composes per-class enumerator ports. This is slice 1 of 3 from task-0325dcf7ee744123b40cf583230c7b6a, split by architect-d46fcb95 on human direction 2026-08-09 because the parent needed 12+ files before a single test against a 10-file hard cap.

Deliverable: packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/recovery-inventory-contract.ts (+ .js bridge) and recovery-inventory.ts (+ .js bridge), focused tests, and the @moe/runner root seam.

MEASURED at 2026-08-09: `find packages apps -type d -name recovery-inventory` returns nothing and no RECOVERY_INVENTORY_* / INVENTORY_ADAPTER symbol exists in any package src. The gap is real.

*** STRUCTURAL FACT THE PARENT DESCRIPTION DOES NOT STATE, measured from packages/runner/package.json: @moe/runner depends on @moe/contracts ONLY. The cursor/generation identity landed in @moe/store (task-5606947a9d7d4f228dc63e6ce4dea69a) and the recovery incarnation landed in apps/daemon (task-684e6972c8c1418f8996ea3edd61f00c). Neither is importable from this package and adding either dependency would invert the package graph. Both therefore enter as CALLER-SUPPLIED OPAQUE REFS that this contract validates for shape and binds by digest, never interprets. ***

Scope: the frozen configured class set; the INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer and the RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN vocabulary; the canonical item shape (class, stable external identity, observed disposition facts, source proof digest); the COMPLETE-or-UNKNOWN coverage proof per class; deterministic ordering and digest across path separators and locale; duplicate-identity and out-of-project/out-of-window refusal; and the aggregate collector that takes a registry of per-class enumerator ports and returns one coverage proof per CONFIGURED class. With no adapter registered every configured class answers UNKNOWN, which is the correct fail-closed answer and is what this slice ships.

NOT in scope: any adapter implementation (slices 2 and 3), scheduler resource rows, adopt/quarantine decisions, project embargo, or tests/fault.

Owned paths: packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/** and the minimal @moe/runner root export/surface-test wiring. This slice is the ONLY one of the three that touches index.ts and index-surface.test.ts; slices 2 and 3 register through the port registry instead.

WARNING measured by the architect: packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts pins the EXACT root namespace against a hand-written EXPECTED_EXPORTS list and a hard-coded `expect(EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length).toBe(116)`. It was ALREADY red on 2026-08-09 from an unrelated in-flight task's exports. Capture the merge-base baseline before editing, transcribe only your own names, and attribute the residual red per the path-attributed-baseline rail.

Consumers (global rail Clause 1): the two adapter slices of this split, and daemon coordinator task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test
definitionOfDone: The aggregate API accepts an exact project tag, an opaque backup cursor/generation ref, an opaque recovery-incarnation ref, recovery-window bounds, and a frozen configured class set, validating each opaque ref for shape and binding it by digest without interpreting it; a malformed project tag or ref refuses with a stable code at layer INVENTORY_ADAPTER before any enumerator runs.

It returns canonical items plus exactly one explicit COMPLETE or UNKNOWN coverage proof per CONFIGURED class - never per returned class - so a class with no registered enumerator answers UNKNOWN rather than vanishing from the report.

An unavailable enumerator, an unsupported provider capability, a truncated or over-limit result, and a missing negative proof each return RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN at layer INVENTORY_ADAPTER with truth UNKNOWN; partial items never upgrade coverage and no path raises an UNKNOWN back to COMPLETE.

Enumeration order and the inventory digest are deterministic across path separators and locale; duplicate external identities and entries outside the exact project or window refuse with their own stable codes rather than merging or being dropped.

Tests deep-equal the frozen class set and code vocabulary against hand-written literals, assert every configured class generated at least one coverage case with a non-zero asserted count, pin the exact code and refusing layer on every refusal, and include a mutation drill proving the coverage handling is reddenable.

The @moe/runner root exposes the contract and aggregate with its type closure, index-surface.test.ts's hand-written list and count literal are updated by hand, and fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test exits 0 with residual red attributed to foreign paths against a recorded baseline.
taskRails: A configured class requires complete enumeration or a verifiable negative proof; an empty list, a quiet process, an absent optional probe, or a mock response is never COMPLETE by itself.

The backup cursor/generation ref and the recovery-incarnation ref are OPAQUE. @moe/runner cannot import @moe/store or @moe/daemon and must not gain either dependency; validate shape, bind by digest, never interpret or re-derive.
Ship no adapter in this slice. Every enumerator is an injected port; the production adapters land in the two sibling slices.
Tests assert the exact stable reason code and the INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer, and assert non-zero generated class coverage.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; this cap is per file, not per task.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED: add one focused suite that imports the intended production surface only through bare `@moe/runner`. Hand-author, rather than derive from the implementation, the four node-side classes `PROVIDER_PROCESS_LAUNCH_LOCK`, `WORKSPACE`, `GIT_INTEGRATION_ON_DISK`, and `ARTIFACT_OBJECT_STAGING`; the exact error/layer/coverage-reason vocabularies; and a non-zero case table for every configured class. Pin request-validation precedence (exact request/version, project tag, backup ref, incarnation ref, inclusive UTC window, frozen non-empty unique configured classes) and assert the enumerator call count stays zero on each refusal. Cover missing/throwing/unavailable/unsupported/malformed/truncated/over-limit enumerators and missing negative proof as per-class `RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN` at `INVENTORY_ADAPTER`, truth `UNKNOWN`; explicit COMPLETE enumeration and empty COMPLETE only with a negative-proof digest; partial items that remain UNKNOWN; wrong class/project/window and duplicate normalized identities with their own exact code/layer; unconfigured ports never called; deterministic items/digest under shuffled input, object-key order, locale-hostile text, and PATH separator variants; digest sensitivity to every semantic basis/fact/proof; and deep immutability. Every sweep asserts its literal expected count and exact generated ID set so zero/filtered cases fail.
implementationPlan.note:
RED PROVEN, not assumed: `npx vitest run --root ../.. packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory` -> 53 tests discovered, 50 failed / 3 passed. Non-zero discovery is itself asserted, so the suite cannot pass by finding nothing.

The 3 that pass are deliberate: they are the sweep non-vacuity guards (`generated every declared refusal case` = 14, `generated every declared UNKNOWN case` = 7 with 7 DISTINCT reasons, `generated every declared item-refusal case` = 4, `generated every declared basis-sensitivity case` = 4). They assert the case TABLES are populated and touch no production symbol, so they are green before the implementation exists by design — that is what makes a later silently-filtered sweep go red instead of passing with zero cases.

Every vocabulary is hand-written from the DoD, never imported-then-echoed: version string, the 4 classes, the single INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer, COMPLETE/UNKNOWN, all 11 error codes in precedence order, all 9 UNKNOWN reasons, both ref kinds.

Coverage of the DoD in this suite:
- Request precedence, 14 cases, each asserting BOTH the exact code AND that the enumerator call count is still 0 (a refusal that runs a port has already touched the disk).
- Registry registering one class twice -> REQUEST_INVALID.
- No adapter registered -> every configured class UNKNOWN/ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED, coverage UNKNOWN.
- One proof per CONFIGURED class, asserted against a 2-class subset where only 1 is registered, so a per-RETURNED-class implementation fails.
- An enumerator registered for an unconfigured class is never called (asserted by call count 0).
- 7 UNKNOWN mappings incl. rejected promise and SYNCHRONOUS throw as separate tests (a `try` around a non-awaited call catches only one of the two).
- Empty COMPLETE admitted only with a negative-proof digest, and the digest is recorded on the proof.
- Item admission: 4 refusals each pinning their OWN code (CLASS_MISMATCH / PROJECT_MISMATCH / WINDOW_MISMATCH x2 edges) with reason ITEM_REJECTED, never a generic COVERAGE_UNKNOWN.
- Both inclusive window edges admitted.
- PATH duplicate that aliases ONLY after separator normalization -> EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE; the mirrored OPAQUE case asserts the opposite, that opaque bytes are NOT separator-normalized and stay distinct. These two together are what stop a blanket backslash rewrite.
- Determinism: shuffled enumerator order, reversed input, fact-record key order, and an explicit code-point-vs-locale ordering case ("Z-upper" before "a-lower", which localeCompare would invert).
- Digest sensitivity: 4 basis fields plus item fact and source proof.
- Deep immutability incl. nested items[0].facts.
- Registry mutated AFTER construction is not observed.
- Repeated concurrent collection is byte-identical.

Not yet green: the suite imports through the bare package root `@moe/runner` and the seam is not published until step 5, which is the ordering the plan requires. Deep subpath imports were not used — the package exports map is exclusive, so a subpath import would not prove the seam a real consumer gets.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the bounded contract and its exact one-line Node bridge. Define version `moe-recovery-inventory/1`; frozen class, coverage, layer, error-code, and UNKNOWN-reason vocabularies; maximum counts/text bounds; immutable input/item/proof/report/failure/port types; and accessor-safe exact-key decoders using the verified runner canonical/shape primitives. Opaque upstream bindings are exact `{kind, ref, digest}` projections with kinds `BACKUP_CURSOR_GENERATION` and `RECOVERY_INCARNATION`; validate bounded NFC text and lowercase SHA-256 but never import or interpret `@moe/store`/`@moe/daemon`. Define an inclusive canonical-UTC recovery window. Make stable identities a discriminated `PATH|OPAQUE` value: normalize only PATH separators to `/` before canonical path validation/deduplication, preserve OPAQUE identity bytes apart from NFC validation, and compare strings by code point rather than `localeCompare`. Items bind class, exact project tag, stable identity, canonical observation time, bounded canonical disposition facts, and source-proof digest. Freeze the precedence vocabulary as `REQUEST_INVALID`, `PROJECT_TAG_INVALID`, `BACKUP_REF_INVALID`, `INCARNATION_REF_INVALID`, `WINDOW_INVALID`, `CONFIGURED_CLASSES_INVALID`, `CLASS_MISMATCH`, `PROJECT_MISMATCH`, `WINDOW_MISMATCH`, `EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE`, then `COVERAGE_UNKNOWN`, all prefixed `RECOVERY_INVENTORY_` and all at `INVENTORY_ADAPTER`.
implementationPlan.note:
Contract landed, plus ONE FILE THE PLAN DID NOT NAME. Scope growth declared here rather than buried.

SPLIT, and why: the contract as first written was 387 physical lines — under the 400 hard cap but 55% over the 250 target, and one edit away from breaching. Split along the seam the module already had: `recovery-inventory-contract.ts` (207) declares the vocabulary and types; `recovery-inventory-shape.ts` (214) decides whether an arriving value is one of them. Each has its exact one-line `.js` bridge. Owned paths go 7 -> 9, still inside the plan's 10-file bound.

DEFECT I INTRODUCED AND FIXED — worth QA knowing the detection method, because a green suite would never have shown it. `identityKey` was written as `` `PATH\0${...}` `` with two LITERAL NUL BYTES instead of the intended space. Symptoms: `grep` reported "Binary file ... matches" on a valid-UTF-8 file, and my first check (`grep -qP '\x00'`) reported no-nul, i.e. the obvious probe LIED. What found it: `perl -ne 'while (/([^\x09\x0A\x20-\x7E])/g) { printf("U+%04X", ord($1)) }'`, which prints code points per line and cannot early-exit on binary detection. Fixed by byte substitution (`perl -i -pe 's/\x00/ /g'`) because the Edit tool cannot match a control character in old_string. Verified afterwards: 0 NUL bytes across all 5 new files, and `diff <(perl -pe 's/\x00/ /g' backup) current` is empty, proving the substitution changed nothing else. Functionally the NUL "worked" as a separator, so tests were green with it in place — this was only ever findable by byte inspection, and it would have made git treat a source file as binary and destroy its reviewability.

CONTRACT CONTENT: version `moe-recovery-inventory/1`; 4 frozen classes; single `INVENTORY_ADAPTER` layer; COMPLETE/UNKNOWN with UNKNOWN as the floor; 11 error codes frozen IN PRECEDENCE ORDER; 9 UNKNOWN reasons; 2 opaque ref kinds; bounds 4096 items / 400 chars / 32 facts. Types are all `readonly`. `recoveryInventoryFailure` and `isRecoveryInventoryFailure` are the only logic left in the contract.

SHAPE CONTENT, and the three decisions a reviewer should attack:
1. `utcSortKey` exists because plain string comparison is WRONG on canonical UTC: `...:00Z` and `...:00.000Z` are the same instant but `.` (0x2E) sorts below `Z` (0x5A), so a lexicographic window bound would have excluded a legitimate edge observation. It collapses both spellings to a fixed-width 17-digit key.
2. `compareCodePoints` iterates the string (yielding code points) instead of using `<` on UTF-16 code units or `localeCompare`. A digest whose item order depends on the host's collation is not a digest, and a surrogate-pair character must sort by scalar value, not by its halves.
3. PATH identities are separator-normalized before comparison; OPAQUE identities are NOT. A blanket backslash rewrite would merge two genuinely distinct provider ids. Both directions are pinned by tests.

`readFacts` handles the one open key set here by reading `Object.keys` and then lifting those keys back through `exactRecord`, so an accessor still never answers and a key added between the two reads cannot enter the snapshot.

NO FORBIDDEN DEPENDENCY: `grep -rn "@moe/store|@moe/daemon"` over this directory matches only the JSDoc sentence explaining why they cannot be imported. `packages/runner/package.json` dependencies remain exactly `['@moe/contracts']` — measured, not assumed.

Typecheck clean. Behaviour is verified in step 5's run, once the seam is published.

implementationPlan.description: Implement `collectRecoveryInventory` and its one-line bridge as a pure async aggregate over an immutable caller-supplied registry tuple—never a mutable module-global registry. Snapshot and validate the entire request and registry before the first await; derive a domain-separated basis digest from version/project/opaque refs/window/configured classes; invoke each configured class exactly once in frozen class order; and never call unconfigured registrations. A missing registration, rejected/thrown port, unsupported capability, malformed/truncated/over-limit result, unverifiable source proof, or missing completeness/negative proof yields that class's exact UNKNOWN proof and cannot be raised later. Validate every returned item before authority use in the frozen order shape → class → project → window → normalized external-identity duplication; structurally valid partial observations may remain inspectable but never count COMPLETE. Require one proof per configured class and non-empty configured input to avoid vacuous `every()`, compute canonical item/proof/inventory digests with code-point sorting, deep-freeze the result, and set aggregate coverage COMPLETE only when the exact configured proof set is COMPLETE. Export a pure registry constructor/fragment type so sibling adapters can be composed by the daemon without editing this aggregate or registering global state.
implementationPlan.note:
`collectRecoveryInventory` + `createRecoveryInventoryRegistry` landed with their exact one-line bridge.

REGISTRY IS AN IMMUTABLE CALLER-SUPPLIED TUPLE, never a module global. `createRecoveryInventoryRegistry` copies the caller's array and freezes both the wrapper and the copy, so a sibling adapter slice composes fragments at the daemon edge instead of importing this aggregate to register into it. A module-global registry was rejected outright: it is order-dependent across concurrent collections and would let another slice change this file's behaviour without editing it. Pinned by a test that pushes into the caller's array AFTER construction and asserts the late entry is not observed.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS, which is the whole correctness argument: the entire request AND the whole registry are read and validated BEFORE the first `await`. Nothing is re-read afterwards, so a hostile record cannot pass validation and then supply different bytes to the digest.

PRECEDENCE is explicit and is the contract, not an accident of control flow: request shape -> project tag -> backup ref -> incarnation ref -> window -> configured classes. A request wrong in two ways always reports the earlier code.

FAIL-CLOSED MAPPING, one proof per CONFIGURED class in frozen class order: unregistered -> ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED; thrown OR rejected -> ENUMERATOR_FAILED (both legs covered — `await` inside `try` catches the sync throw and the rejection, and the two are separate tests because a `try` around a non-awaited call would catch only one); UNAVAILABLE/UNSUPPORTED -> their own reasons; unreadable answer -> RESULT_MALFORMED; over MAX_RECOVERY_INVENTORY_ITEMS -> RESULT_OVER_LIMIT; `complete !== true` -> RESULT_TRUNCATED; empty-and-complete with no negative proof -> NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING. Nothing raises an UNKNOWN back to COMPLETE — a class's outcome is decided once and never revisited by a later class succeeding.

ITEM ADMISSION runs in a FIXED order — shape, class, project, window, then normalized identity duplication — so a hostile item cannot choose which code refuses it. An item-level refusal carries its OWN code (CLASS_MISMATCH / PROJECT_MISMATCH / WINDOW_MISMATCH / EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE) with reason ITEM_REJECTED, never a generic COVERAGE_UNKNOWN, and the class drops to UNKNOWN rather than the item being silently dropped.

TWO ANTI-VACUITY GUARDS in the aggregate coverage decision, because `every()` on an empty list is true: aggregate COMPLETE requires `proofs.length === configuredClasses.length` AND `configuredClasses.length > 0` AND every proof COMPLETE. A proof list that lost a class cannot report COMPLETE.

DIGESTS: `basisDigest` is domain-separated by version and binds project tag, both opaque refs (kind+ref+digest), window and configured classes. `inventoryDigest` binds the basis, the canonically ordered items, and each proof's own digest. Ordering is frozen-class-index then `compareCodePoints` on the normalized identity key, so enumerator order, caller key order and host locale cannot move it. Result is `deepFreeze`d.

SIZE, DECLARED RATHER THAN QUIETLY ACCEPTED: this file is 364 physical lines. That is under the epic's 400 hard cap but over the 250 target. I extracted `readBasis`'s repetitive refusal blocks behind a `refuse()` helper, which recovered lines without obscuring the precedence order that tests pin. I did NOT split further: a fourth production module plus its bridge would take this task to 11 owned paths against the plan's explicit 10-file bound, and breaching a stated hard bound to improve on a stated target is the wrong trade. Flagging it rather than hiding it — if a sibling slice grows this file, it must split before 400. `packages/runner/src/index.ts` is 261 for the same reason (the repo's own remedy, a `surface/*-surface.ts` module, also costs 2 files).

Suite: 53/53 green, typecheck clean.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review found TWO real defects in my own code. Both fixed and pinned; neither had a failing test before review, which is the point.

DEFECT 1 — SILENT FACT DROP VIA `__proto__` (the serious one). `readFacts` accumulated validated facts into a plain `{}`. `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":1}')` creates an own DATA property that `Object.keys` reports, but assigning that key onto `{}` is swallowed by the inherited setter. Probed it directly before believing it: copying `["__proto__","ok"]` into `{}` yields `["ok"]`; into `Object.create(null)` yields both. So an adapter could ship a fact that passed validation, vanished from the record, and never entered the digest — the exact silent drop this contract exists to forbid.
What actually happened downstream was worse to diagnose: the SHARED `exactRecord` helper accumulates into `{}` too, so the key was dropped there first, and my later read of `snapshot["__proto__"]` returned `Object.prototype`, which failed the value check and rejected the item. Net behaviour was fail-closed BY ACCIDENT, through two interacting drops, with a refusal that named nothing about the real cause.
Fix: `readFacts` now lifts each key out of its own property DESCRIPTOR into an `Object.create(null)` accumulator, so a `__proto__` fact is preserved as a real key and IS bound to the digest. Also removed the `{...entry, facts: {...entry.facts}}` re-spread in `buildReport`, which was a second place the same drop could have been reintroduced. Pinned by a test that asserts the item is admitted, the key survives into `report.items[0].facts`, AND the inventory digest differs from the same item without the smuggled fact.
NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY, and flagged for whoever owns it: `exactRecord` in `packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-shape.ts` has the same `{}` accumulator. It is unreachable there because every other caller passes a FIXED key list containing no `__proto__`. It is not my owned path and I did not touch it.

DEFECT 2 — `readRegistry` read `.registrations`, `.class` and `.enumerate` as plain property accesses after only an `isStrictRecord` check. `isStrictRecord` rejects proxies and odd prototypes but NOT accessors, so a getter would have been invoked during validation, and a registration carrying unknown extra fields was accepted. Fixed by routing both through `exactRecord`, which is exact-key and data-property-only. Two new tests: an extra-field registration refuses with REQUEST_INVALID, and a hostile `get class()` refuses with the getter's read counter asserted to be exactly 0 — proving it was never invoked rather than merely out-read.

MUTATION DRILLS — 4 run against the FINAL bytes (re-run after the hardening edits, not just the earlier ones), each killing its named test and not unrelated red:
- D1 missing-registration branch -> COMPLETE: kills "answers UNKNOWN/ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED...", "emits one proof per CONFIGURED class...", AND the public-root "composes the recovery-inventory seam through the root..." (3 failed / 229 passed).
- D2 missing-negative-proof branch disabled: kills "maps an empty COMPLETE claim with no negative proof..." (1 failed).
- D3 one class removed from the frozen vocabulary: kills the value-pinned vocabulary test, the per-configured-class test, and the public-root test (3 failed) — this is the non-vacuity guard proving a shrunk case set cannot pass quietly.
- D4 identity dedup disabled: kills "refuses duplicate identities that alias only after PATH separator normalization" (1 failed).
RESTORE PROVEN BY CHECKSUM, not by `git checkout`: these files are UNTRACKED, so git could not have restored them. `sha256sum -c` over all 7 files reports OK after every drill.

METHOD NOTE worth keeping: one verification run reported success while finding ZERO tests, because my shell cwd had drifted into the package directory and `--root .` then pointed at the wrong tree. Caught it from the `filter:/include:/exclude:` banner rather than a pass/fail line. Every count in these notes is from a run re-anchored at the repo root.

CHECKLIST ITEMS CLEARED BY INSPECTION, no change needed: concurrency (pure over inputs, no shared mutable state; concurrent collection tested byte-identical), registry mutation after construction (frozen copy, tested), sync throw AND rejected promise (separate tests, since one `try` shape catches only one), empty/duplicate/unknown class sets, over-limit lists (4097 read bound, >4096 refused), 400-char text bound, deep freeze incl. the null-prototype facts record, and unconfigured ports never invoked.
ACCEPTED LIMITATION, declared rather than hidden: a port returning a thenable that never settles will hang `collectRecoveryInventory` forever. There is no timeout because a timeout needs a clock, and a clock would make this aggregate non-deterministic and un-replayable. Cancellation belongs to the daemon caller.
DESIGN NOTE: a class with a rejected item returns `items: []`, so partial observations are not carried into the report. The plan's wording permits

QA audit by qa-b2df68b9, 2026-08-09 ~15:25Z. Approving. Full evidence; the approval summary is the short form.

## Gate re-run by me, twice, unnarrowed

The recorded `verification.command` is the DoD's own command with no `--exclude`, no test filter, no `|| true`. Re-run before and after my mutation drill:
```
pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck  -> exit 0
pnpm --filter @moe/runner test       -> 43 files / 1366 tests passed, exit 0
```
**No residual red at all.** The `packages/runner` typecheck failure that was live an hour ago (`src/scope/scope-git.test.ts` TS2305/TS2339 on `parseRefListing`/`listRefs`, untracked) has cleared — that foreign in-flight task landed its implementation. Worth stating because two other tasks disclosed it as their foreign red today; it is gone, not hidden.

## DoD coverage

**1 — refuse before any enumerator runs.** The refusal sweep pins the code *and* asserts `workspace.calls.length === 0` (`:193`), so "before any enumerator runs" is proven by the port never being called rather than by argument. 14 declared cases including malformed project tag, both opaque refs, window shape, and the three `configuredClasses` failures.

**2 — one proof per CONFIGURED class.** `report.proofs.length` is asserted against `RECOVERY_INVENTORY_CLASSES.length` (`:245`) — the production constant, not a test-local copy. The root-surface test drives the pair that *is* the protocol: a registered class proves `COMPLETE` off a negative proof while a configured-but-unregistered class yields `["GIT_INTEGRATION_ON_DISK", "UNKNOWN", "ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED"]` rather than vanishing, and `report.coverage` is `UNKNOWN`.

**3 — nothing upgrades an UNKNOWN.** `unknownClass` and `rejectedClass` both construct `truth: "UNKNOWN"` unconditionally; there is no branch anywhere that rewrites a proof's truth after construction. `admitItems` returns `COMPLETE` only at one site, and only after the negative-proof check.

**4 — determinism and identity.** `:459` refuses duplicates that alias only after path-separator normalization; `:478` keeps opaque identity bytes distinct when they differ only by separator (the inverse property, which is the one people forget); `:524` orders by code point rather than locale collation.

**5 — sweep counts and layer.** Every table asserts an exact non-zero cardinality: `CASES` 14, `UNKNOWN_CASES` 7, `ITEM_CASES` 4, `SENSITIVITY` 4, plus `UNKNOWN_CASES.filter(reason === "RESULT_MALFORMED").length === 2`. The `INVENTORY_ADAPTER` layer is pinned through `const LAYER` at `:33` used in 7 assertions, several inside the table loops, so it lands on every refusal rather than on one sample. I checked this specifically because a single textual occurrence of `INVENTORY_ADAPTER` in the file looked thin at first grep; it is a hoisted literal, not missing coverage.

**6 — root seam.** `index.ts` exports the value surface and the full type closure by explicit name, not `export *`, with a comment recording that as a reviewed decision. `index-surface.test.ts` went **135 -> 147** and exactly **12** value names were hand-added — I counted the added entries against the delta. The architect's warning said the literal was `116`; it had since moved to 135 under other tasks, and the worker transcribed only their own names onto the current value rather than restoring a stale one. The count and the namespace are cross-checked by a separate "no loss and no addition" assertion, so a miscount could not pass by itself.

## Mutation drill — run by me, and it is the rail-1 property

I chose the drill after checking what is actually reachable. The two vacuity guards in the coverage computation — `proofs.length === basis.configuredClasses.length` and `basis.configuredClasses.length > 0` — sit behind an upstream refusal (`configuredClasses: []` already refuses with `RECOVERY_INVENTORY_CONFIGURED_CLASSES_INVALID`, `:172`), so they are defence-in-depth and a mutant there would survive *correctly*. Drilling them would have produced a false finding.

The property that genuinely gates authority is task rail 1: an empty list is never COMPLETE by itself. Mutating `if (admitted.length === 0 && negativeProofDigest === null)` to `if (false)`:
```
FAIL > coverage protocol > maps an empty COMPLETE claim with no negative proof
       to COVERAGE_UNKNOWN/NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING at INVENTORY_ADAPTER
AssertionError: expected 'COMPLETE' to be 'UNKNOWN'
Tests  1 failed | 55 passed (56)
```
One test red, and it is the one whose name states the rail. That is the defect that would otherwise let a quiet enumerator launder silence into proven-complete coverage.

**Restore discipline, because these files are untracked and `git diff` cannot verify them.** Backup held outside the repository, `sha256sum` before and after: `3d3de745…dec1cdce` both sides, MATCH. `git log -1` still `ffa39d6`, confirming no completion hook swept the mutation window. Full gate re-run green after restore.

## Two things recorded, neither a rejection reason

**Nothing is committed.** `git status` shows `?? packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/` plus `M index.ts` and `M index-surface.test.ts`; no commit bears this task id and the new directory is untracked. The global rail is explicit that the absence of a task-id commit is never a rejection reason, so I verified against the working-tree bytes — which are exactly the bytes the gate ran against, established by hash across the drill. Stating it so nobody later reads this approval as certifying committed bytes: it certifies the working tree at 15:25Z.

**`recovery-inventory.ts` is 378 physical lines** (`grep -c ''`). Contract 207, shape 223, test 615. Task rail 5 and epic rail 5 both say "target <=250, split before 400", so 378 is compliant — but it is 22 lines from the hard bar, and the two sibling adapter slices register through this aggregate. The next task that needs to touch it will breach 400 rather than approach it. Not a defect today; a note for whoever plans slices 2 and 3, since the cheapest moment to split is before someone is mid-feature.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 7 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Chosen: two focused production modules (closed codec/vocabulary and aggregate), their mandatory one-line bridges, one focused test, and the existing root seam. This is seven files—above the preferred five but below the hard ten-file cap—and is the minimum honest shape: omitting a bridge fails the existing runtime sweep; folding codec plus async aggregation into one source risks the per-file 250/400 cap; moving behavior tests into the already-large root surface test is not focused TDD; splitting publication into another task would leave the pure surface unreviewed and create a second collision on the same root files. Upstream backup/incarnation data is represented as exact opaque projections, rejecting both dependency inversion and a local reimplementation of store/daemon authority. The node-side class vocabulary is four combined classes because scheduler resources are explicitly out of scope and the two sibling adapter slices each name exactly two classes. The recovery window is an inclusive canonical-UTC observation interval, while the backup cursor/generation remains opaque. PATH and OPAQUE identity variants avoid blindly rewriting provider IDs. Registration is immutable and caller-injected; mutable global registration was rejected because it is order-dependent, race-prone, and conflicts with this task's injected-port rail. Sibling adapters should export registry fragments and the daemon consumer composes them; they must not edit this aggregate despite stale wording in their descriptions.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Fresh exploration found no recovery-inventory directory or RECOVERY_INVENTORY/INVENTORY_ADAPTER symbols. `packages/runner/package.json` depends only on `@moe/contracts`, confirming that store backup and daemon incarnation shapes cannot be imported. Verified reusable primitives are `packages/runner/src/canonical.ts` (`canonicalDigest`, `deepFreeze`, NFC/timestamp checks), `packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-shape.ts` (accessor-safe exact records and bounded dense lists), and `packages/runner/src/platform/{platform-contract,linux-observation}.ts` (frozen vocabularies and one explicit UNKNOWN verdict per configured boundary). The real upstream projections are `packages/store/src/backup-generation-contracts.ts::BackupGenerationManifest` and `apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation-contract.ts::RecoveryIncarnationBinding`; this task binds only caller-supplied `{kind,ref,digest}` projections. The authoritative design hash was reverified as 1D9D1EC97D3F07247FBBC088045E0BA2FD6DA8307F10A9026C55106419383191. `index.ts` was clean at 215 lines during exploration; the root value count was 135, not the stale 116. The shared HEAD moved repeatedly, so all counts/hashes must be remeasured. `index-surface.test.ts` had +54 foreign uncommitted lines from WORKING task-5855a9c6b8da4a428dd0e75ed9ae36d1. Runner typecheck was exit 0; runner tests were red only in active task-078af6f181484dd99d1bf9008b4cf731's untracked Claude runtime-pin work and its missing bridge. Existing runtime-entrypoint coverage automatically requires each new production `.ts` to have the exact sibling `.js` bridge and performs a real Node package-root probe.
planningNotes.risks: The main operational risk is shared-file capture: never touch or pathspec-commit `index-surface.test.ts` while task-5855's bytes are uncommitted. The final package gate cannot use repo-wide path attribution to excuse task-078's runner-local red; wait for it to land. The main semantic risks are vacuous COMPLETE from an empty configured set/empty proof, a port throw escaping uncoded, a partial class being upgraded after another port succeeds, locale-dependent order, unsafe blanket backslash normalization of opaque IDs, accessors mutating the registry during await, and duplicate identity aliases after PATH normalization. Validate/snapshot before awaits, distinguish PATH from OPAQUE, require exact proof cardinality, and keep UNKNOWN monotone. The sibling task descriptions mention editing this aggregate to register adapters; later plans must amend that stale wording to compose immutable fragments at the daemon edge, avoiding ownership collisions and module-global authority.
